A.name: Claude Code + Claude subscription, no other keys
A.headline: Claude Code on a Claude subscription -- you're already getting routing discipline on it. OpenRouter adds a second, cheaper lane on top.
A.body: Undercut routes within Anthropic's own tier ladder (haiku → sonnet → opus → fable) on your existing subscription -- that's real, non-trivial value on its own: the escalation rubric still catches over-escalation within that ladder, and Pro's real-time pooled testing and effort-level tuning still apply to Anthropic's tiers specifically. Your subscription alone doesn't reach the biggest dollar swings -- openweights tiers run 5-10x cheaper again than Anthropic's own cheapest tier on the task categories where they hold up, per our own cost data.
A.openrouter_framing: Additive, not a replacement. You don't have to leave Claude Code or your Claude subscription -- the unlock is connecting OpenRouter as a second, API-billed lane alongside it, the same pattern Undercut already uses for its own internal subagent routing. Your subscription keeps handling whatever it already handles well; OpenRouter access is what lets the same routing logic also reach the tiers your subscription can't. Connect OpenRouter (one click, your own account, your own billing) and nothing about your subscription changes -- it's additive, never a replacement, and never implied to be inferior. We still do not recommend the unofficial ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy workaround as a way to reach other vendors from inside Claude Code itself -- it's ToS-gray, fragile, and could break without notice; the OpenRouter connect flow is the supported path.
A.honesty_caveat: This is the lower-value-ceiling segment of the four on your subscription alone, and we say so plainly rather than overselling it. We also never compare this to Undercut's own subscription pricing or unit economics on this page -- that's Anthropic's pricing to explain, not ours to characterize.

connect_openrouter.cta_label: Connect OpenRouter -- your account, your billing
connect_openrouter.helper_text: Adds a second lane on top of your Claude subscription. Nothing about the subscription lane changes, and declining keeps you on your current setup permanently -- not a nag state.

B.name: Cursor / Windsurf / Copilot
B.headline: Cursor, Windsurf, or GitHub Copilot -- reach the tier your subscription doesn't include.
B.body: Your native subscription already includes multi-vendor frontier-lab access (Claude, GPT, Gemini) -- that part isn't Undercut's value-add. What Undercut adds: evidence-based escalation logic on top of whatever's already available, plus reaching openweights tiers (DeepSeek, GLM, and similar) that native subscriptions don't include at all.
B.openrouter_framing: Unlocks a tier you don't have. Add an OpenRouter key in your tool's own BYOK settings specifically to reach the cheap openweights tier -- this is presented as unlocking access your subscription doesn't include, not as a generic 'add a key' instruction. Additive on top of what you already have; your existing multi-vendor access through the tool's own subscription is untouched.
B.honesty_caveat: The multi-vendor frontier-lab access you already have is not something Undercut is adding -- we're only claiming the part that's genuinely new: the openweights tier and the routing logic on top of it.

connect_openrouter.cta_label: Connect OpenRouter -- unlock the openweights tier
connect_openrouter.helper_text: Adds the openweights tier your subscription doesn't include. Your tool's native multi-vendor access keeps working exactly as it does today.

C.name: OpenCode / Continue.dev / Cline / Aider / Roo Code / Kilo Code
C.headline: OpenCode, Continue.dev, Cline, Aider, Roo Code, or Kilo Code -- already on API billing, so this is pure upside.
C.body: As of 2026-01-09 (formalized in Anthropic's Consumer ToS on 2026-02-19), Claude Pro/Max subscription auth tokens are blocked in third-party tools. Practically, anyone routing model traffic through one of these tools today is already paying per-token API rates for whichever vendor -- there's no subscription being used here to give up. Adding an OpenRouter key to reach openweights tiers is pure upside, zero tradeoff.
C.openrouter_framing: Zero-downside, pure upside. This is the strongest, cleanest pitch of any segment: already on your tool paying API rates? Add an OpenRouter key and there's no downside -- only savings.
C.honesty_caveat: This segment's story only holds because there was never a subscription being used here to trade away -- it's not a special Undercut trick, it's a fact about how these tools already bill.

connect_openrouter.cta_label: Connect OpenRouter -- pure upside, no downside
connect_openrouter.helper_text: There's no subscription lane here to protect -- this is straightforwardly cheaper access on top of the API billing you already have.

D.name: Zed
D.headline: Zed -- bundled Zed Pro subscription; OpenRouter compatibility unverified for your editor.
D.body: Zed bundles its own Zed Pro subscription and cannot use a personal Claude subscription at all, regardless of Undercut.
D.openrouter_framing: Unverified for your editor. Whether Zed's own BYOK settings can reach OpenRouter specifically was not confirmed in our research pass -- we're flagging that openly rather than asserting it works. Check Zed's own provider settings directly before assuming this path is available to you.
D.honesty_caveat: We'd rather tell you we don't know than guess. This is the one segment where we're explicitly withholding a specific recommendation until it's verified.

connect_openrouter.helper_text: We don't show a connect button for this segment -- Zed's own OpenRouter BYOK support is unverified, so we'd rather point you at Zed's provider settings than assert a path that might not exist.

unresearched.headline: We haven't specifically researched your tool's provider setup yet.
unresearched.body: Our compatibility research (last updated 2026-09-14) covered Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, the open/BYO-model group (OpenCode, Continue.dev, Cline, Aider, Roo Code, Kilo Code), and Zed. It didn't cover every tool Undercut's free skill works with. Rather than guess which segment your setup falls into, we're telling you plainly that we don't know yet.
unresearched.openrouter_framing: No claim either way, with one exception that generalizes: if your tool bills you per-token with no subscription in the mix, the Segment C story (adding an OpenRouter key is pure upside) most likely applies to you too. If you're on a subscription for this tool, we don't yet know how it interacts with OpenRouter or other provider keys.
unresearched.honesty_caveat: We'd rather say 'not yet researched' than assign you a segment we can't back up.
